name: DividedSplitting.exists_congruenceGroup_inv_eq_one_sub
summary: Y² = 0, so 1 − Y is a unit; its inverse fixes ϖ̄·1.

steps.claim: Y² = 0, so Y is nilpotent (of index at most 2: the hypotheses allow Y = 0): lifting the entries to integral adeles X, ϖ̄·Y = 0 says ϖ⁻¹X is integral entrywise (reduction_levelModulus_eq_zero_iff), so every entry of Y² is a sum of products of two multiples of ϖ, hence 0 modulo M². So 1 − Y is a unit (IsNilpotent.isUnit_one_sub).
steps.lean:
(IsNilpotent.isUnit_one_sub ⟨2,
  by choose X e using (reduction_surjective _ <| Y · ·)
     simp_all [-e, ← e, ↓← ext_iff, mul_apply, sq, ← map_mul, ↓reduction_levelModulus_eq_zero_iff,
       mul_mul_mul_comm, mul_mem,
       Finset.sum_eq_zero]⟩)

steps.claim: Take A = (1 − Y)⁻¹ as an element of the congruence group, using the identity of step 2.1.
